climateNote: Dayton's humid continental climate (NOAA 30-year normals) means summer humidity routinely pushes indoor levels above 60% — past the EPA's 30–50% ideal — while winter brings freeze-thaw cycles, ice dams, and condensation in closed-up homes.
heroAnswer: Dayton's freeze-thaw winters and humid summers make mold a year-round problem — ice-dam attic growth in winter, basement seepage after spring storms. With roughly three-quarters of homes built before 1980, hidden moisture problems are common across the Miami Valley. We serve Dayton with free inspections, transparent pricing, and photo-documented work. Every job fixes the moisture source first.
housingNote: Roughly three-quarters of Dayton homes were built before 1980, with many downtown and inner neighborhoods dating before 1950. Older roofs, aging plumbing, and decades of small unrepaired leaks make hidden mold common — especially in the city's brick duplexes and rental stock.

moldStory: Dayton combines one of the oldest housing stocks in the Miami Valley — roughly three-quarters of homes predate 1980, with many downtown and inner neighborhoods built before 1950 — with freeze-thaw winters that drive ice dams and attic moisture, and humid summers that feed basement and crawl-space mold. The Great Miami River floodplain adds periodic water-intrusion events, and the city's aging brick duplexes and rental stock often hide long-term moisture problems behind walls.
